title: The Body of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The body of Christ means that believers are joined to Christ and to one another as members of one body. Each member belongs, needs the others, and is called to serve for the good of the whole church.
summary: The body of Christ means that believers are joined to Christ and to one another as members of one body. Each member belongs, needs the others, and is called to serve for the good of the whole church.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Head of the body, and believers live from Him. He gives life, unity, direction, and growth to His people as they serve one another in love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture describes the church as the body of Christ to show both unity and diversity. Believers are many members, yet one body in Christ. No member is meant to live detached from the rest.

The body image also confronts pride and despair. No member may say, “I do not need you,” and no member should believe, “I do not belong.” God places members in the body according to His wisdom.

The body grows as each part works properly. Ministry is not limited to a few visible people. Christ gives grace to the whole body so believers may strengthen, encourage, serve, and build one another up.

Because Christ is the Head, the body must receive its direction and life from Him. Unity without submission to Christ becomes human organization, but unity in Christ becomes living fellowship.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often feel useless, unseen, or disconnected in the church. This doctrine tells the weak, disabled, quiet, wounded, and overlooked that they are not accidental parts of Christ’s body.

It also corrects consumer Christianity. Church is not a performance watched by isolated individuals. It is a living body where believers belong to Christ and are responsible to love and serve one another.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Live as a member of Christ’s body, not as a disconnected spectator. Receive care when you are weak, offer service where God gives grace, and honor members whose gifts or struggles look different from yours. Ask Christ to make you a faithful part of His body.
